transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thanks for seeing me. Um, well, I'm an electrician, and I guess I'm just here because... well, I've been being a little extra thorough at work lately. Probably a bit too thorough, if I'm being honest. 

I just like to make sure everything is perfect, you know? It's important to do a good job. But lately, I keep going back over things. Like, I'll check the breakers, make sure the labels are exactly right, check my torque marks... I even take photos of the panels before I leave. And sometimes, even after I've driven away, I'll turn the truck around and go back to a site just to double-check. 

It's just that a simple install is starting to take me a lot longer than it used to. And my boss and the other guys are starting to notice. I just want to do things right, but I guess it's getting a little out of hand. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you can help with?
Are these extra checks and double-checks causing you a lot of anxiety or stress?

Um, I wouldn't say a lot of stress, no. I mean, I manage it okay, I definitely don't want to make a huge deal out of it. 

It's just... well, even after I know for a fact I checked a panel or a disconnect, this thought just keeps barging in on me. Like, what if I missed one loose neutral? Or what if I left something that could spark and start a fire? 

I try really hard to just shake it off, I really do, but it kind of... it just follows me all the way home. I guess that does make me a little tense sometimes. But I mean, anyone in my line of work would worry about safety, right? I'm just trying to be a good employee. Does that sound normal to you?
Would you say that these thoughts about missing something or causing a fire are unwanted, or are they something you intentionally think about to be thorough?

Well, I definitely don't try to think about it on purpose. I mean, I want to be thorough, but it's more like... the thought just kind of pops up on its own. 

Like I said, I'll know for a fact that I checked the panel, but then this idea just barges in. Like, "What if you missed a loose neutral?" or "What if something sparks and causes a fire?" And it's not like I want to sit there and dwell on it. I really try to just push it out of my head and move on with my day. But it's stubborn, you know? It just kind of tags along with me, all the way home sometimes. 

But I mean, I'm sure it's just because I care about doing a good job, right? It's pretty normal to want to be careful when you're working with electricity, don't you think? I'm not crazy for having those thoughts, am I?
Are these thoughts about potential electrical hazards affecting your personal relationships or daily activities outside of work?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it's ruining my life or anything like that. I mean, I still get things done. But... I guess it is bleeding over a little bit, if I'm being completely honest. 

Like, my schedule at work is slipping a bit. Jobs that I should really be able to knock out in one visit are turning into, you know, callbacks or me just going back for extra checks on my own time. And I think it's starting to cost me some confidence with my clients, and I'm definitely losing time I should be spending training the apprentices. I don't want to let them down, you know? 

And, um, outside of work... well, I guess I have been skipping some things I used to enjoy doing in the evenings. Sometimes I'm just still tied up reviewing a job in my head, or I'm sitting there worrying about whether I need to drive back out to a site. So I just stay home instead. 

But I mean, a lot of guys take their work home with them, right? Especially when it's something as important as electrical safety. It's not that unusual to want to be responsible, is it? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
Do you feel like these thoughts about electrical hazards are a part of who you are, or do they feel like they're coming from outside of yourself?

Um, that's a... that's a really good question, actually. I guess I haven't thought about it exactly like that before. 

I mean, I definitely don't think they're coming from outside of me, like, you know, hearing voices or anything crazy like that. I'm definitely not crazy. It's just my own brain, my own thoughts. 

But at the same time, it doesn't really feel like... *me*, either? Like, the real me is the guy who knows I did the job right the first time. The real me knows the panel is secure. These thoughts, they just kind of... they just sort of hijack my brain for a bit. It's like my brain is just being a little too cautious on my behalf, you know? 

So I guess they're mine, but they're the part of me that just wants to be a really, really safe electrician. That's a normal way to look at it, right? I mean, it makes sense that my brain would just be trying to protect people, doesn't it?
Do you find yourself needing to arrange things in a specific or symmetrical way, even when it's not necessarily related to your work as an electrician?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I like things to be neat, sure. Like, my tools are organized in my truck so I can find them, but that's just... that's just being professional, right? 

I don't really get hung up on making things perfectly symmetrical or anything like that at home. My wife would probably tell you I leave my shoes in the middle of the hallway half the time, so I'm definitely not a neat freak or anything. 

So, yeah, no, I don't really have any issues with arranging things. That's a good thing, right? Like, that means it's really just about the safety stuff at work, which is understandable. Don't you think?
Do you feel distressed or uncomfortable when these thoughts about electrical hazards pop into your head?

Um, well... I guess I wouldn't say I'm, like, completely distressed. I mean, I can handle it. I'm a professional, you know? But... yeah, I suppose it is a little uncomfortable. 

It's just that, um... even after I know I checked a panel, or, you know, a disconnect, and I know I did it right... this thought just keeps sort of barging in on me. Like, what if I missed one loose neutral? Or what if I left something just slightly off that could start a fire? 

And I really try to just shake it off, you know? I tell myself I did a good job. But... it just kind of follows me. Like, all the way home. It just sits there in the back of my mind. 

But I mean, that's just because I care about my work, right? It's better to be a little uncomfortable than to let someone's house catch fire. That's a good way to look at it, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
Are these thoughts and double-checks significantly interfering with your ability to enjoy your free time or spend time with family and friends?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it's *significantly* interfering, you know? I mean, I'm still functioning fine. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it has been getting a little bit in the way lately. Just a little. 

Like, with work, my schedule has been slipping just a bit. Because, well, jobs that I really should finish in one visit, they kind of turn into... callbacks, I guess you could say. Or just extra checks on my end. I just want to be absolutely sure everything is safe, but... I think it is starting to cost me a little bit of client confidence, which I really hate to admit. And it cuts into my time training the apprentices, too, because I'm so focused on reviewing my own work.

And, um, as for my free time... yeah, I suppose I have been skipping a few things I used to enjoy doing after work. It's just hard to relax when I'm still kind of... tied up reviewing a job in my head, or worrying about whether I need to drive back to a site and check a connection one more time. 

But I'm really just trying to be responsible and do right by my customers, you know? That's a good quality for a contractor to have, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
Do you feel compelled to repeat certain actions or behaviors outside of your work, such as washing your hands or checking locks, in a specific way or a certain number of times?

Um, no, no, not really. I mean, I lock the front door at night, of course, just like anyone else would. You know, just to be safe. But I don't, like, stand there and check it a dozen times or anything crazy like that. 

And hand washing... I mean, my hands get pretty dirty on the job, pulling wire and all that, so I wash them when I get home. But just regular washing, you know? Not scrubbing them raw or doing it over and over. 

So, yeah, outside of work, I'm pretty much just a regular guy. I don't really have any of those kinds of habits. That's a positive sign, right? Like, it means I'm keeping things pretty normal at home, don't you think?
Do you feel like these thoughts about electrical hazards are forcing their way into your mind, even when you're trying to think about something else?

Well, yeah... um, I guess it's a lot like what I was mentioning earlier. It's just that, even when I'm absolutely certain I checked a panel, or I know the disconnect is totally fine... the thought just kind of pushes its way in anyway. 

Like, I'll be driving away, trying to listen to the radio or think about what I'm going to make for dinner, and suddenly I'm just worrying that maybe I missed one loose neutral, or maybe I left something just a tiny bit loose that could spark a fire. 

And, you know, I really do try to just shake it off and focus on something else. I tell myself I did it right. But it just stubbornly follows me all the way home, no matter what I try to think about instead. 

It's not like I'm losing my mind or anything, though! I just... I have a hard time turning work off. That's pretty normal for someone in the trades, right? Just having a really strong sense of responsibility... you see that a lot with your other patients, don't you?
Do you feel like these thoughts about electrical hazards are popping into your head without you wanting them to?

Well, um, I guess it's basically what I was just saying... it's not like I'm trying to think about it, you know? It's more like... even after I know for a fact that I checked a panel, or I'm positive the disconnect is good to go, the thought just kind of barges in anyway. 

It's just this nagging feeling that maybe, just maybe, I missed one loose neutral wire, or left something that could start a fire. And I really do try to push it away. I try to shake it off and just enjoy my drive home, but... it just kind of tags along with me. 

But I mean, that's just because I care about my work, right? It's better to care too much than not enough, don't you think? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for people.
Do you feel like these thoughts about electrical hazards are inconsistent with your own values or the kind of person you think you are?

Um, no, I wouldn't say that. Honestly, I feel like it's... it's kind of the opposite? I mean, I'm an electrician, so making sure things are safe and up to code is exactly the kind of person I want to be. It's my job, you know? 

I'd feel a lot worse if I was the kind of guy who just slapped some wires together and didn't care if a house caught fire. So, worrying about hazards... I feel like it just shows I take pride in my work. Sure, maybe it gets a little frustrating when I can't just drop it on the drive home, but it's coming from a good place. 

It just means I'm a really conscientious worker, right? That's a good trait to have, wouldn't you say?
Are these thoughts about electrical hazards affecting your ability to sleep at night?

Oh, no, not really. I mean... um, my sleep is actually pretty good, thankfully. By the time I get home and have dinner, I'm usually so beat from being on my feet all day that I just kind of crash. 

I don't lie awake staring at the ceiling worrying about breaker panels or anything like that. I mean, sure, maybe a thought pops up right as my head hits the pillow sometimes, but I just... I just remind myself that I did solid work and then I fall right to sleep. 

That's a really good sign, right? Like, if I'm sleeping okay, it means I'm keeping things pretty well balanced, don't you think?
Would you say that these unwanted thoughts about electrical hazards are causing you a lot of emotional pain or distress?

Well, um, "distress" might be a strong word. I mean, it's not like I'm breaking down or anything like that. 

I guess... maybe it gets a little annoying sometimes? Like, I'll be trying to watch a game with my kids, and my brain is just kind of buzzing in the background about whether I torqued a lug nut enough. But it's not like it ruins my whole night. I just kind of sigh and try to focus back on the TV. 

It's just part of the job, you know? Everyone brings a little bit of their work home with them, right? I'm sure even you think about your patients after you leave the office sometimes, don't you? It's just normal stress from wanting to do things right.
Do you spend more than an hour a day thinking about electrical hazards or checking your work?

Oh, um... an hour a day? No, I don't think it's that much. I mean, sure, I might double-check a panel before I leave a job site, just to be absolutely certain everything is buttoned up right. But that's just a few extra minutes here and there, you know? 

I wouldn't say I spend hours dwelling on it. Like I said, it's just a fleeting thought every now and then when I'm off the clock. I'm pretty good at leaving work at work, for the most part. 

Spending an hour every single day just obsessing over it... that would be a bit much, wouldn't it? I'm definitely not doing that. I think I manage my time pretty well, don't you?
Are these thoughts and behaviors related to electrical hazards causing problems in your relationships with your family or friends?

Well, um... with my family, no, not really. I mean, they know I work hard. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, maybe it's affecting my work schedule a little bit more than I let on earlier? 

It's just... sometimes a job that should only take one visit ends up turning into, you know, a callback. Or I spend extra time checking things, and it puts me behind. I think it's starting to cost me a little bit of client confidence, which I really hate to admit. And I don't get as much time to train the apprentices because I'm so focused on making sure my own work is perfect. 

And... well, I guess I have been skipping some things I used to enjoy after work. Sometimes I'm just still tied up reviewing a job in my head, or I'm worrying about whether I need to drive back to a site just to be absolutely sure. 

But I'm just trying to be thorough, you know? It's better to be safe than sorry when you're dealing with electricity. That's the right attitude to have, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job.
Do you feel like these thoughts about electrical hazards are causing you significant emotional distress?

Um... well, we did kind of touch on this a minute ago, right? I mean, "significant emotional distress"... that sounds really intense. Like I said before, it's not like I'm crying or having a breakdown over it. 

I guess... I mean, it's a little frustrating sometimes when I get stuck in my head, but it's not like it's tearing me apart inside. It's just... stress. Normal, everyday stress from trying to be a responsible guy. 

I don't think that counts as "significant distress," does it? I feel like I'm handling it okay, for the most part. I'm not crazy for just wanting to be careful, right?
Are these thoughts about electrical hazards making it difficult for you to complete daily tasks or enjoy activities outside of work?

Well, um... I guess we sort of talked about this just a little bit already, didn't we? 

I mean, as far as daily tasks go... it's mostly just my work schedule that's slipping a little bit. Like I mentioned, sometimes a job that I really should finish in one visit ends up turning into, you know, extra checks or a callback. And... well, I hate to say it, but it is starting to cost me a little bit of client confidence. Which isn't great, obviously. And I don't get as much time with the apprentices as I'd like. 

And outside of work... yeah, I guess I have been skipping a few things I used to enjoy doing in the evenings. Sometimes I'm just... still tied up reviewing a job in my head, or I'm worrying about whether I need to go back to a site to check on something. 

But I'm just trying to be a responsible business owner, you know? I want my clients to know they can count on me to do things right. It's perfectly normal to want to do a good job and be thorough, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing things the right way.
Are these thoughts about electrical hazards interfering with your relationships with friends or causing you to avoid social activities?

Oh, um... I know I keep bringing it back to work, I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself too much. I hope I'm answering your questions the right way. But... yeah, as far as friends and social stuff goes, it really just ties right into what I was just saying about skipping things I used to enjoy after work. 

Like, if the guys want to get together, I usually end up bowing out now. Because my business schedule is slipping from those one-visit jobs turning into extra checks and callbacks, I just feel like I don't have the free time. And honestly, even if I do try to go out and be social, I'm not very good company. I'm usually just sitting there tied up reviewing a job in my head, or worrying about whether I need to excuse myself and go back to a site to look at a panel again. 

So I guess I have been avoiding social activities, yeah. But it's mostly just because I need to fix the fact that it's starting to cost me client confidence, and I really need to make up for that lost time with my apprentices. Anyone would prioritize getting their business back on track over hanging out with friends if things were slipping a bit, wouldn't they? I'm just trying to do the responsible thing.
Do you feel compelled to perform any specific rituals or behaviors, such as counting or tapping, when you are not working or thinking about electrical hazards?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. I don't do anything like... counting or tapping, or, you know, anything like that. 

When I'm actually able to put the work stuff out of my mind, I'm just... normal. Just a regular guy. I hope that makes sense? I mean, I wouldn't want you to think I'm doing all these strange little habits all day long. It really is just about making sure my electrical jobs are safe and done right. 

So, no counting or anything. That's a good sign, right? That I'm not doing any of that other stuff?

Um, no, no, not really. I mean, I lock the front door at night, of course, just like anyone else would. You know, just to be safe. But I don't, like, stand there and check it a dozen times or anything crazy like that.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's thoughts are intrusive
doctor.question: Do you feel like these thoughts about electrical hazards are forcing their way into your mind, even when you're trying to think about something else?

target_item.name: Obsessions
target_item.manifestation: Even after I know I checked a panel or a disconnect, this thought keeps barging in on me that maybe I missed one loose neutral or left something that could start a fire, and I try to shake it off but it follows me all the way home.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the thoughts about electrical hazards feel like they are forcing their way into the patient's mind (intrusive and unwanted), which corresponds directly to the definition of obsessions.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah... um, I guess it's a lot like what I was mentioning earlier. It's just that, even when I'm absolutely certain I checked a panel, or I know the disconnect is totally fine... the thought just kind of pushes its way in anyway. 

Like, I'll be driving away, trying to listen to the radio or think about what I'm going to make for dinner, and suddenly I'm just worrying that maybe I missed one loose neutral, or maybe I left something just a tiny bit loose that could spark a fire. 

And, you know, I really do try to just shake it off and focus on something else. I tell myself I did it right. But it just stubbornly follows me all the way home, no matter what I try to think about instead. 

It's not like I'm losing my mind or anything, though! I just... I have a hard time turning work off. That's pretty normal for someone in the trades, right? Just having a really strong sense of responsibility... you see that a lot with your other patients, don't you?

Well, um, I guess it's basically what I was just saying... it's not like I'm trying to think about it, you know? It's more like... even after I know for a fact that I checked a panel, or I'm positive the disconnect is good to go, the thought just kind of barges in anyway. 

It's just this nagging feeling that maybe, just maybe, I missed one loose neutral wire, or left something that could start a fire. And I really do try to push it away. I try to shake it off and just enjoy my drive home, but... it just kind of tags along with me. 

But I mean, that's just because I care about my work, right? It's better to care too much than not enough, don't you think? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for people.

Um, no, I wouldn't say that. Honestly, I feel like it's... it's kind of the opposite? I mean, I'm an electrician, so making sure things are safe and up to code is exactly the kind of person I want to be. It's my job, you know? 

I'd feel a lot worse if I was the kind of guy who just slapped some wires together and didn't care if a house caught fire. So, worrying about hazards... I feel like it just shows I take pride in my work. Sure, maybe it gets a little frustrating when I can't just drop it on the drive home, but it's coming from a good place. 

It just means I'm a really conscientious worker, right? That's a good trait to have, wouldn't you say?

It's just part of the job, you know? Everyone brings a little bit of their work home with them, right? I'm sure even you think about your patients after you leave the office sometimes, don't you? It's just normal stress from wanting to do things right.

Spending an hour every single day just obsessing over it... that would be a bit much, wouldn't it? I'm definitely not doing that. I think I manage my time pretty well, don't you?
